messages:
Jordan (acct): FYI — Acme reported failures after a deploy this morning. their pipeline sees "embedding dimension mismatch" errors intermittently and a billing spike. forwarding their note: 'we used embed-small-v2 (1536d) but some calls return 1024d'.
Maya: ugh. do we have a deploy id/time from Acme? any example request/response? :thinking_face:
Jordan (acct): they attached logs and a minimal repro. says it started ~07:12 UTC. repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'X-Client-Tenant: tenant-acme' \n  -d '{"model":"embed-small-v2","input":["a","b","c"]}'
```
response for second request gave 400 + message: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024"
They also saw increased p50/p95 latency around same time.
Sam: thanks. can we get the exact model id they used (alias vs pinned)? sometimes folks float aliases. also need request ids from responses.
Jordan (acct): they said they pinned to "embed-small-v2@2026-02-25" in their config. included one response id: resp_20260225_9a3f. attached billing spike screenshot.
Eli: I'll check cache logs + routing for tenant-acme around 1911110000-1911113000. initial thought: cache key normalization bug from last month caused model_variant to be omitted when building prefix key for embeddings cache. that could let a 1024-d embedding vector (quantized variant) be served for a 1536-d request if prefix reused.
Tara: wait, how would different dims be the same key? caching isn't supposed to store raw vectors across dims. do we currently include dims in the key? I thought we did.
Eli: we normally include model_id + quantization + dims + tenant_prefix. but the bug was: when request used alias (e.g., embed-small-v2 -> embed-small-v2-quant) the cache-key builder used canonical model name but omitted quantization flag in some batch codepath. and the batching aggregator normalizes prefixes incorrectly when inputs are mixed lengths. so two issues might be compounding.
Maya: can you paste the relevant log lines if you find them? I want to reproduce locally with our small harness.
Eli: found this in runtime logs for tenant=tenant-acme: 
```
[1911112231] INFO cache_lookup key="tenant-acme|embed-small-v2|quant=none|dim=1536|prefix=sh:abc123" result=MISS
[1911112232] INFO cache_lookup key="tenant-acme|embed-small-v2|quant=quant8|dim=1024|prefix=sh:abc123" result=HIT serving_from_cache=true serving_dim=1024
[1911112232] WARN serve_mismatch request_dim=1536 served_dim=1024 request_id=resp_20260225_9a3f
```
so you can see prefix bits are identical (sh:abc123) — prefix is tenant-managed and was reused by the customer across different model variants. the missing quant flag in the first key path makes the 1024 value accessible via the 1536 request path in certain racey sequences.
Sam: ok that explains mismatch errors. what about the latency and billing spike?
Eli: when cache returns wrong-dimension embeddings we detect mismatch and fall back to regenerating embeddings which ends up double-costing: first cached hit then regeneration. some requests get counted twice in billing meters because both the cache hit and the regeneration are billed to the tenant. the fallback path also adds extra latency.
Tara: do we have a repro? I can write a small script that toggles model alias to quant variant then send two back-to-back batch requests with same prefix and mixed inputs.
Maya: here's quick repro I used locally based on customer input:
```python
import requests
H={'Authorization':'Bearer X','X-Client-Tenant':'tenant-acme'}
# write prefix header to simulate tenant-managed prefix
for m in ['embed-small-v2','embed-small-v2-quant']:
    r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', headers=H, json={'model':m,'input':['alpha']})
    print(m, r.status_code, r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
# now batch mixed and hit rapid sequence
r1 = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', headers=H, json={'model':'embed-small-v2','input':['a','b']})
r2 = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', headers=H, json={'model':'embed-small-v2-quant','input':['c','d']})
print(r1.status_code, r2.status_code)
```
This reproduces a 400 on the first client's pipeline when run fast enough. slower runs often avoid the race.
Jordan (acct): Acme is asking for a timeline and whether data was exposed between their model variants. they also asked if this caused any other tenants to see similar billing anomalies.
Eli: we audited other tenants — saw a handful of similar events but only with tenants that used tenant-managed prefixes and both quant + non-quant variants. scope is limited. not a cross-tenant data leak — prefix reuse was tenant-scoped. still high severity for affected customers.
Maya: immediate mitigation options?
Sam: short-term: block serving cached embeddings when dims != request dims (we already do check but need stricter early key separation), and reject ambiguous alias-to-variant cache hits. also add a soft rate-limit so fallback regeneration isn't double-billed until we patch meters.
Eli: I've pushed a hotfix branch that forces cache keys to include the full model_variant string in all codepaths, and adds an extra guard to reject quick-hits where dims mismatch. rollout plan: canary on eng-runtime pool in us-west-2 in 10m, monitor errors and billing. if green promote to 100%.
Tara: can you add a unit test and an integration test showing batch mixing path? I'll help with test vectors.
Eli: yes. test added. also instrumented logs to emit cache_key and served_dim for 30m for faster triage.
OpsBot: deploy scheduled: runtime/patch/embed-cache-key-fix -> canary (us-west-2) at 1911112300, health-checks every 30s.
:rocket:
BillingBot: noticed unusual billing delta for tenant-acme: +$1.2k estimated from duplicated generation events between 1911112100-1911112400. created billing ticket BT-9842 and applied temporary credit to tenant-acme account.
Jordan (acct): Acme appreciated the quick credit. they want a postmortem and timeline. can we also provide recommended client guidance so they don't hit this again?
Maya: draft guidance: 
- prefer pinned model SHAs rather than floating aliases for mixed-variant usage
- avoid reusing tenant-managed prefixes across different model variants 
- if you must reuse prefixes, ensure model_variant included in prefix metadata or use separate prefixes per model
I'll draft docs and send to Jordan for customer-facing email.
Eli: follow-ups for eng:
- merge hotfix and promote after 30m of canary green
- add e2e test in CI that simulates batch mixing + alias -> variant rename
- add billing meter dedupe for immediate duplicate-generation events within 1s window
I'll open tickets.
Sam: thanks team. Jordan — I'll be your single point to Acme; we'll send timeline + remediation + postmortem once we have canary results.
Jordan (acct): thanks all. Acme says they can postpone wider rollout until fix is in. they want a short blurb for their infra team.
Maya: on it, will post draft in this thread in ~30m. :memo:
